pattern: Data table with multi-level headers (WAI Tables tutorial: tables with multi-level headers, technique H43 headers/id), inside a focusable labelled scroll region. Not an ARIA grid: expand and sort buttons are native buttons in the Tab order. The field list is a group of labelled lists with toggle-button move handles (keyboard drag-and-drop pattern, as Sortable List and Dashboard Grid) and live-region announcements; member filters are disclosure panels with a native checkbox fieldset.

roles.role: cell, associated with every header through the headers attribute
list / listitem (native), each list named by its title (aria-labelledby)
button (native); the handle is a toggle (aria-pressed), the filter toggle a disclosure (aria-expanded, aria-controls)
search input (type=search), fieldset with a visually hidden legend and native checkboxes, role=status count, buttons

aria.value: Ids of the column group headers, the member or total header, the value header, and the row header
true while the data source request runs
ascending or descending on the sorted header (the corner is ascending by default)
Virtual mode only: total rows (header rows included) and each rendered row's position
The group path ('North, '), so a row header names its group even when the group row is scrolled away

aria.element: move handle / aggregate select / remove / search

aria.value: true while the field is grabbed (keyboard or single pointer)
Assertive: grabbed, moved, dropped, cancelled, not allowed, load failed. Polite: sorted by {column}, sorting cleared.

keyboard.action: Moves to the scroll region (arrow keys scroll it), then through the corner sort button, column expand buttons, value sort buttons, and row expand buttons in reading order.
Toggles the group; the first expansion loads its children (aria-busy). Focus stays on the button (restored after re-rendering, also in virtual mode).
Toggles the row member order between ascending and descending labels; announces 'Sorted by {column}, ...'.
Sorts rows within each group by that column: descending, then ascending, then off (label order); announces the sort.
Grabs the field (aria-pressed=true) and announces '{field} grabbed. {area}, position {position} of {count}.'; pressed again drops it.
Moves it up or down within its list; announces '{area}, position {position} of {count}.'
Moves it to the end of the previous or next list (Fields, Filters, Columns, Rows, Values; mirrored in RTL), skipping lists the field is not allowed in.
Moves it to the start or end of its list.
Cancels: the lists return to the layout; announces 'Move cancelled. {field} is back in {area}.'
Drops the field and moves focus on (leaving the field list also drops).
Opens or closes the member filter panel (focus moves to its search field).
Closes the panel without applying and returns focus to the filter toggle.

focus: The scroll region is a tab stop with a focus ring. Expand and sort buttons keep focus after the table re-renders (and in virtual mode the focused row stays rendered). During a keyboard or single-pointer move the grabbed field's handle keeps focus (the lists re-render around it). Opening a filter panel focuses its search field; Apply, Cancel, and Escape return focus to the filter toggle.
notes: Multi-level headers are associated with every data cell through headers/id (H43), including column groups, totals, and value headers.
Totals differ by weight and a strong rule, not by color alone (1.4.1).
Moving fields never requires dragging (2.5.7): keyboard grab and arrow keys, or click the handle and then click the target list.
The scroll region is keyboard scrollable and headers stick, so content reflows at 320 px without loss (1.4.10).
Loading and error states are text in the table body; aria-busy marks the table while loading.
knownCaveats: Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
Screen readers differ in how much of a long headers list they read for each cell; very deep column nesting produces long announcements.
Pointer drags in the field list are not announced; keyboard and single-pointer moves are.
In virtual mode, table navigation commands of screen readers see only the rendered rows (aria-rowcount gives the total).
